The letter from Friend of the Court came on a Tuesday. Four thousand, one hundred eighty dollars behind.
My hours got cut in August. I've been paying what I can.
I'm not trying to get out of taking care of my daughter. I'd pay double if it meant I saw her more than every other weekend.
I didn't want a sermon. I didn't want to call my mama. So I opened this app my cousin kept sending me.
There's a box called Ask for Help. I typed what I was actually thinking.
It didn't tell me I was wrong for being mad. It told me what to do with it.
And it told me to call the child support office about my hours. Which, honestly, I'd been avoiding.
Then I asked the question I really needed answered.
Keep it to one topic. In a text. So you can think before you answer. I read that line probably twenty times.
Before bed I filled out the check-in. How are you doing. I didn't dress it up.
Next morning, somebody had written back.
On my break I pressed play on one of the reels.
I called the office on my lunch. They told me how to ask for a review since my income changed. It's not fixed. But it's moving.
I sent her one text. Just the money, nothing else. She answered. No argument.
Saturday, I picked up my daughter. We went to the park. I didn't look at my phone once.
